title: Period and Graph of y = -sin(pi*x/3)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine the fundamental period of y = -\sin(\pi x / 3) and describe its graph, including the effect of the negative sign.

steps.title: Calculate the Fundamental Period
steps.explanation: Divide 2*pi by the angular frequency pi/3 to obtain the period B = 6.
steps.why: As x goes from 0 to 6, the angle pi*x/3 goes from 0 to 2*pi.

steps.title: Analyze the Amplitude and Vertical Reflection
steps.explanation: The amplitude is |A| = 1, and the negative coefficient reflects the standard sine wave across the x-axis.
steps.why: Multiplying a function by -1 reflects its graph vertically across the horizontal axis.

steps.title: Find Quarter-Period Landmarks on [0, 6]
steps.explanation: With quarter-period 6/4 = 3/2, the reflected wave decreases from (0, 0) to a minimum at (3/2, -1), crosses (3, 0), rises to a maximum at (9/2, 1), and returns to (6, 0).
